## Status

Frozen pre-outcome protocol. No mortality status, follow-up distribution or
exposure-outcome association was examined before specification freeze. All
planned pre-outcome audits were completed before the corresponding annotated Git
tag was created.

## Research question

Among US adults aged 20 years or older, is a higher baseline concentration of
C-reactive protein associated with subsequent all-cause mortality?

## Design and target population

This is a retrospective cohort analysis of continuous NHANES participants linked
to the NCHS public-use mortality file. The target population is the civilian,
noninstitutionalized US population aged 20 years or older represented by the
pooled 1999–2000 through 2009–2010 cycles.

Eligible participants must have a valid baseline CRP result, a positive applicable
MEC examination weight, eligibility for public-use mortality linkage and valid
follow-up information. Participants with confirmed pregnancy at examination will
be excluded because pregnancy changes CRP physiology and makes baseline BMI less
comparable. Participants aged 20–44 years with indeterminate pregnancy status will
be retained in the primary analysis and excluded in a sensitivity analysis.

## Exposure

Baseline CRP will be converted from mg/dL to mg/L by multiplication by 10. The
primary exposure will be `log2(CRP)`, so its coefficient represents a doubling of
CRP. A restricted cubic spline will assess whether the adjusted association is
nonlinear.

NHANES released below-detection observations using the detection limit divided by
the square root of two. These values will be retained in the primary analysis.
Sensitivity analyses will substitute the nominal detection limit and separately
exclude below-detection observations.

## Outcome and time scale

The outcome is all-cause mortality through 31 December 2019. The primary time
scale is elapsed time from the mobile examination center examination to death or
administrative censoring. Age will be modeled flexibly as a baseline covariate.

## Target estimand

The target estimand is the adjusted hazard ratio for all-cause mortality per
doubling of baseline CRP. This is an adjusted prognostic association, not a causal
effect of intervening on CRP. If nonlinearity is supported, pre-specified contrasts
from the spline curve will supplement the single linear hazard ratio.

## Adjustment strategy

The primary model will adjust for baseline age, sex, race and Hispanic origin,
educational attainment, smoking status, body mass index, diabetes, hypertension,
prevalent cardiovascular disease and survey cycle. Covariates are selected from
substantive knowledge and will not be screened by univariable p-values.

Three nested presentations will be used:

1. demographic adjustment for age, sex, race and Hispanic origin, and cycle;
2. the fully adjusted primary model;
3. the primary model plus family income-to-poverty ratio as a sensitivity analysis.

The nested models describe how adjustment changes the CRP estimate. They are not
competing models selected according to statistical fit.

## Survey design

All primary inference will incorporate the MEC weight, sampling stratum and
primary sampling unit. Pooled weights will use `WTMEC4YR / 3` for 1999–2002 and
`WTMEC2YR / 6` for 2003–2010.

## Missing baseline covariates

After excluding 1,135 participants with confirmed pregnancy, 27,755 participants
remain eligible for the primary cohort. Following explicit recoding of numeric
*refused* and *don't know* responses, 26,818, or 96.62%, have complete primary-model
covariates. Adding income-to-poverty ratio reduces complete records to 24,683,
or 88.93% of the primary eligible cohort.

Multiple imputation will be a sensitivity analysis. Fifty imputed datasets are
planned; each will be analyzed with the same survey-weighted Cox model, and
estimates will be combined using Rubin's rules. CRP, mortality status, follow-up
time and survey design identifiers will not themselves be imputed.

## Effect modification

Sex and age group, 20–64 versus 65 years or older, will be evaluated separately as
pre-specified secondary effect modifiers. Formal interaction tests and confidence
intervals will be reported. Subgroup findings will not replace the overall primary
analysis.

## Sensitivity analyses

Planned sensitivities include exclusion of CRP greater than 10 mg/L, alternative
handling of below-detection CRP, exclusion of early deaths, adjustment for family
income-to-poverty ratio, multiple imputation, an alternative age specification and
diagnostic comparison of weighted and unweighted estimates.

## Reporting

Reporting will follow STROBE and the RECORD extension where applicable. Completed
checklists will accompany the final report. NHANES analytic guidance will govern
the complex survey design.

## Specification freeze

The three pre-outcome audits have confirmed exposure availability, linkage
eligibility, category coding, final missingness, pregnancy counts, participant
uniqueness and cohort flow. The protocol and statistical analysis plan rendered
successfully and underwent final review before the annotated specification tag.
Any subsequent change must be documented prospectively as a numbered amendment.
